title: Bounded-memory resumable transfer and replica safety
summary: Large media moves through ranged StorageByteSource/StorageByteSink adapters and a resumable transfer engine. COPY, VERIFY and COMMIT are deliberately separate states so an interrupted or merely copied object is not confused with durable completion.
invariants: Transfer memory is governed by bounded chunks rather than whole-object size.
Sink flush occurs before durable checkpoint progress advances.
Two-generation checksummed checkpoints allow fallback from a torn newest checkpoint.
Resume is fenced by source identity so stale evidence cannot continue against a changed local source.
COPIED is not VERIFIED and VERIFIED is not COMMITTED.
The last safe replica may not be evicted merely because another unverified or disposable copy exists.
Before restoring a COPYING transfer, a capable remote sink may reconcile the checkpoint offset against provider-authoritative resume evidence.
Partial remote acknowledgement advances only the acknowledged prefix and reopens the source at that exact offset; the suffix is retransmitted.

provenance.claim: Implements bounded transfer, provider-authoritative resume reconciliation, partial-ack replay, checkpoint and verification contracts.
Regression proves provider evidence can repair a stale/torn local checkpoint before resumed transfer.
